generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The change from `int` to `long` for `sendSegmentNumber` and `receiveSegmentNumber` is necessary to handle the wrap-around behavior of TCP sequence numbers, which are 32-bit unsigned integers. This change ensures that the sequence numbers do not overflow beyond their maximum value. The introduction of the `incrementUintSegmentNumber` method is a good approach to handle the wrap-around logic. It correctly uses modulo operation with `0xFFFFFFFFL` to ensure the sequence number wraps around when it exceeds the 32-bit unsigned integer limit. The changes in `handleTCP`, `completeTCPWrite`, and `handlerRemoved` methods are consistent with the new data type for sequence numbers, ensuring that all operations involving these variables are updated accordingly. The update to the `logTCP` method signature to accept `long` instead of `int` for sequence numbers is necessary to maintain consistency with the rest of the codebase. The changes in the `TCPPacket.writePacket` method to cast `segmentNumber` and `ackNumber` back to `int` before writing them to the buffer are correct, as TCP headers require 32-bit integers.

review_comment: We should produce a 5G file and try to read it using Wireshark just to be double-sure.
@normanmaurer I'll have time today to look into this and address any issues I find.

Found 2 issues directly related to this PR while using Wireshark to look at the generated 5GB pcap. Those will be addressed.

Noticed two other issues present in 4.1.

1. If the payload is larger than 65495 for TCP, the length field in the IP packet is incorrect due to the length being a ushort. UDP will have a similar problem.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/155cec08-767f-4efc-a2c5-c9c04718bd75)
2. When the PcapWriteHandler is attached to a TCP server, the FIN messages have incorrect segment and ack numbers. 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/236c3109-558d-4fa2-8cce-5fa05503ebc0)


I will try to find the time to address these here with unit tests

For TCP, the payload can just be split into multiple PCAP entries. 
For UDP, I imagine it could just log that it received too large of a payload.
Alright, all of the above have been handled. Tested large PCAP files and those show correctly in Wireshark now.
